news.text: 7 December saw Naughty Dog and Sony release platforming triumph *Crash Bandicoot: Warped* for the **PlayStation** across Europe, capping a golden Christmas for the 32-bit console. Sending the spinning marsupial hopping through time-bending portals from prehistoric swamps to medieval castles, the sequel added tiger-riding dashes along the Great Wall of China and plane dogfights against biplanes. Tight controls and vibrant cartoon visuals convinced millions of festive shoppers that spinning bandicoots were vastly superior to Italian plumbers.
news.youtube: Crash Bandicoot 3 Warped original PS1 commercial 1998

news.text: 11 December saw Nintendo release *The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time* on the **Nintendo 64** across Europe, triggering retail bedlam on British high streets. Widely hailed by gaming publications as the crowning achievement of the medium, stores exhausted their allocations within hours as frantic parents scrambled for golden cartridges. Lucky children who unwrapped it on Christmas morning promptly disappeared into the Water Temple, their festive holidays consumed by grappling hooks and iron boots.

news.text: 13 December saw the WWF visit Vancouver for *Rock Bottom*, headlined by a bone-crunching **Buried Alive** match between "Stone Cold" Steve Austin and The Undertaker. Just as the Deadman seemed destined to dump Austin into the grave, Kane erupted from the shadows and used a yellow construction backhoe excavator to pour a massive shovel of earth over The Undertaker, handing Austin the victory and a spot in the 1999 Royal Rumble. Meanwhile, Mankind defeated The Rock with the Mandible Claw, only for corporate boss Vince McMahon to reverse the ruling on an absurd technicality.
news.youtube: Stone Cold vs Undertaker Buried Alive Rock Bottom 1998

news.text: 16 December saw American and British air and naval forces commence **Operation Desert Fox**, launching a punishing four-day bombing campaign against military and security infrastructure across Iraq. Triggered by Saddam Hussein's continued expulsion and obstruction of United Nations weapons inspectors (**UNSCOM**), cruise missiles struck command bunkers and alleged chemical research sites. Sceptics in Washington noted that the fireworks conveniently coincided with the opening salvos of President Clinton's congressional impeachment debate, inspiring cynical comparisons to the Hollywood movie *Wag the Dog*.
news.youtube: Operation Desert Fox strikes Iraq December 1998 news report

news.text: 19 December saw the United States House of Representatives vote to impeach President **Bill Clinton** on charges of perjury and obstruction of justice arising from the Monica Lewinsky scandal. Becoming only the second president in American history to suffer impeachment after Andrew Johnson in 1868, the bitter partisan vote in Washington exposed deep cultural and political fractures across the republic. Clinton remained characteristically unbowed in the Rose Garden, confident that the required two-thirds majority in the upcoming Senate trial would never be mustered.
news.youtube: House impeaches President Bill Clinton December 1998

news.text: 25 December saw the **Spice Girls** equal an iconic pop milestone by scoring their third consecutive UK Christmas number one single with the bittersweet farewell ballad *Goodbye*. Matching the record set by **The Beatles** between 1963 and 1965, the single was the group's first release following the shocking departure of Geri Halliwell earlier that summer. Performing as a four-piece, the group proved that their chart momentum remained robust, leaving festive rivals like *Chef's Chocolate Salty Balls* stuck in the runners-up spot.
